lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constructing linear and exponential functions from data
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: constructing linear and exponential functions from data

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2700(0.97)^t, with t in years. What does 0.97 represent?
choices: the fraction of value retained each year, 0.97, meaning a 3% annual loss
the total value lost over the asset's life
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the value of the asset when it was new, $2700

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, 7) and (3, 15). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 8, 16, 32, 64. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.

items.prompt: A population of 1600 grows by 2% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 29 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
A stays ahead permanently because 29 is larger than 3.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 1400(0.9)^t, with t in years. What does 1400 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $1400
the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.9, meaning a 10% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, 13) and (4, 25). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 6, 12, 24, 48. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.
